dedupe_keys.name: african internet exchange system axis project

description: This policy case covers the African Union's programme to keep Africa's internet traffic on the continent by helping countries set up internet exchange points and regional exchanges. Grounded in the African Regional Action Plan on the Knowledge Economy and endorsed by the AU Executive Council, the African Internet Exchange System project provided capacity building and technical help for national exchanges, then studies and workshops to grow regional exchanges and carriers, a certificate curriculum on exchange technology and model regulation for cross-border interconnection in the East African Community and the Southern African Development Community. It was co-financed by the EU-Africa Infrastructure Trust Fund and the Government of Luxembourg, with LuxDev as lead financier, and the Internet Society ran the national and regional workshops. Reports credit the project with six new national exchanges within its first two years, training in 28 countries for more than 500 people, and milestones such as the Senegal exchange in 2017; the Internet Society counts 41 new active exchanges in Africa between 2012 and 2023. Coverage: African Union member states, from about 2012. Format and access: AU and Internet Society web pages, free. Caveats: no independent evaluation was found, and the counts mix the project's own results with wider growth. Simulation uses: network flow and latency effects of local interconnection, and capacity planning for regional exchanges. Related records: the Kenya and Nigeria exchange impact study, the PCH IXP directory and PeeringDB.
